articleBody:
- [ ] Zoning designation and accessory unit rules — Confirms your parcel allows secondary living units or attached guest suites.
- [ ] Emergency egress window specifications — Ensures sleeping quarters meet strict dimension standards for safe emergency exits.
- [ ] Minimum ceiling height verification — Checks that finished ceilings throughout the suite meet code standards after drywall installation.
- [ ] Dedicated smoke and carbon monoxide alarms — Required in all sleeping rooms and adjoining hallways for life-safety compliance.
- [ ] Electrical panel load calculation — Determines whether an auxiliary subpanel or main service upgrade is needed for kitchen appliances and HVAC.
- [ ] Plumbing sewer tie-in path — Maps out how bathroom and kitchenette waste lines will connect to your main home sewer connection.
- [ ] Independent heating and cooling plan — Specifies how the suite will maintain comfortable temperatures without overtaxing the primary AC.
- [ ] Accessible doorway and walkway clearances — Guarantees wider doorways and level thresholds for comfortable long-term mobility.

How to use this checklist:
Gather these details before drawing construction layouts or hiring subcontractors. Verifying life-safety regulations, plumbing tie-ins, and zoning allowances upfront prevents costly teardowns or permit delays. When you are ready to design a compliant, comfortable suite in the Tampa Bay area, reach out to Bay City Remodeling & Bathrooms at 813-362-0114.
